newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London recover Monday's slide.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London recover Monday's slide.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks recovered yesterday's fall in quiet London trading on Tuesday, on the back of stronger U.S. bonds, a firmer Wall Street performance, and hefty futures premiums in Hong Kong, traders said.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index ended 55.32 points higher at 13,511.58, compared with yesterday's close of 13,464.35.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index ended at 13,456.26, down from the previous close of 13,517.56.

"Movement is really confined to the laggards," Merrill Lynch salesman Mark Driver said. He summed up the day's trading as "second tier buying", adding that traders would be concentrating on utilities and stocks which have not moved.
One UBS trader said the HSBC was the only interesting mover of the day with a rise of 1.15 percent.

HSBC is one of three foreign banks to be given licences to handle yuan business this month, Shanghai Star newspaper reported on Tuesday. Up to now, foreign banks were restricted to foreign currency business only.
Traders were divided over whether this report, or the bank's recent consolidation, was responsible for the attraction of capital.
"HSBC is going through a consolidation recently," Driver said. "The bank will be firmer on this news;" he added.
Traders expected the Hong kong stocks to continue their gradual uptrend tomorrow.
